title: Optical Frequency Domain Imaging of Ex vivo Pulmonary Resection Specimens: Obtaining One to One Image to Histopathology Correlation
protocol: Turn on imaging system.
Set and record imaging parameters (rotational speed, pullback speed, image acquisition rate, etc).
Attach catheter to rotary junction and pullback device.
Spin catheter and check for image quality.
Adjust system alignment and offset as needed.
Place a tabletop disposable absorbent pad on the benchtop.
Set lung specimen on the pad.
Consult the pathology department to ensure all resection margins have been assessed and documented if the specimen is from a patient.
Identify the bronchial airway entering the resection specimen at the hilum.
Remove visible mucus within the airway using a syringe bore.
Attach a longer segment of plastic tubing to the syringe bore if necessary, to suction deeper within the airway.
Palpate the exterior surface of the specimen to identify the lesion of interest.
Navigate through the bronchial tree with a fine metal probe until near the lesion of interest.
Open the airway along the probe until the lesion is visible or palpable under the airway mucosa.
Remove any blood or mucus from the airway mucosa overlying the lesion using a cotton-tipped applicator.
Place the OFDI catheter above the airway mucosa and obtain an image to confirm the lesion is underlying the airway mucosa.
Identify a high-quality imaging region of interest for histology correlation.
Select the region of interest in the airway based on previous imaging findings.
Choose two points on the tissue along the desired line of imaging.
Space dots no more than 1.5 cm apart.
Dip a fine tipped open bore needle into the tissue marking dye.
Wipe excess ink off the outside of the needle with gauze.
Puncture the tissue perpendicular to the airway mucosa at the chosen point.
Repeat steps for the second point on the airway mucosa.
Use a cotton tipped applicator to carefully remove excess ink if it runs over the mucosal surface away from the puncture site.
Remove mucus or blood on the surface of the airway mucosa with a cotton tipped applicator, if present.
Place the OFDI catheter over each ink mark and image.
Ensure marks appear as focal disruptions within the tissue structure with overlying highly scattering particles and underlying rapid signal attenuation.
If ink mark(s) are not visible on OFDI, repeat steps 4.3 to 4.7 for the non-visible marks.
Proceed to step 5.3 if ink marks are visible with OFDI.
Place the catheter parallel to the two ink marks on the airway mucosal surface such that the catheter optics overlie the tissue beyond the first ink mark.
Anchoring the proximal end of the catheter with a lightweight object and securing the distal end can help reduce motion artifacts.
Collect an OFDI pullback.
View the OFDI pullback images to ensure both ink marks are visible in imaging.
Check for motion artifacts in the OFDI pullback images.
If the marks are not visible, repeat steps 5.1 to 5.4.
Place a green ink dot on the airway mucosal tissue to orient the beginning of the imaging scan, 0.3 cm away from the first ink mark in the imaging pullback.
Remove tissue encompassing the two black ink marks and green ink mark.
Trim tissue to fit into a standard histology processing cassette.
Fix tissue in 10% formalin for at least 48 hours if cutting fresh tissue is difficult.
Place fixed tissue in a histology processing cassette.
Process tissue in a tissue processor.
Embed tissue in paraffin parallel to the two black ink marks on the airway surface.
Face the paraffin block until either an ink mark or entire tissue section is visible.
Cut one 5 μm thick section and mount onto a glass slide once both black ink marks are visible.
Continue cutting and mounting 5 μm thick sections every 50 μm until the black ink marks or tissue ends are no longer visible.
Follow standard hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining protocols to stain and coverslip slides.
Re-interpolate volumetric datasets so that a single 2D image bisects both ink marks for correlation with histology if necessary.
Use ImageJ or other image processing software for re-interpolation of images if required.
Examine adjacent sections/slides if the ink is not readily visible.
